**Verdict**

No HIGH findings. I would not call D-1 fully closed yet because there are two MEDIUM closure items in the XLSX format-overlay boundary.

**MEDIUM 1: XLSX import can create unresolved format overlays**

`cellXfs` styles are applied by converting `xf.num_fmt_id` directly with `legacy_from_u32` and setting the overlay, without checking that custom IDs resolve in `FormatTable`: [lib.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io-xlsx/src/lib.rs:279). The high-ID guard only applies to declared `<numFmt>` entries: [styles_import.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io-xlsx/src/read/styles_import.rs:55).

Empirical result: `<xf numFmtId="999999999">` with no matching `<numFmt>` imports successfully as `Custom(LEGACY_PEER, 999999835)` with no format string. Saving to `.qbook` then reloading fails at the qbook overlay resolver: [qbook_format.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io/src/qbook_format.rs:1752).

**MEDIUM 2: XLSX export accepts unregistered custom overlay IDs**

The exporter includes overlay-used custom IDs in translation even if absent from `workbook.formats()`: [umya_export.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io-xlsx/src/write/umya_export.rs:147). Missing format-code entries allocate a numFmtId anyway: [umya_export.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io-xlsx/src/write/umya_export.rs:225). But `<numFmt>` declarations are emitted only from `workbook.formats()`: [umya_export.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io-xlsx/src/write/umya_export.rs:553).

Empirical result: an overlay bound to `Custom(PeerId(777), 0)` with no `FormatTable` entry exports an `<xf numFmtId="164">` but no `<numFmt numFmtId="164">`; reimport produces an unresolved overlay.

**LOW: version coupling is documented but not enforced**

`WORKBOOK_SCHEMA_VERSION`, `FormatIdWire` serde shape, and `OPLOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` are pinned separately. Current behavior is okay, but a future `FormatIdWire` shape change has no single test forcing both qbook and oplog schema bumps.

**Passes**

The full arc probe passed: multi-peer `.qbook` save/load preserved IDs, `oplog.bin` had the `QLOL` header, first XLSX export reported exactly 2 multi-peer flattens, format codes survived import, reimported IDs collapsed to `LEGACY_PEER`, second XLSX export reported 0 flattens, and final qbook save/load was byte-stable.

Step-7 carryover also passed: synthesized pre-step-4 raw Loro `RegisterFormat { id: 14 }` loads at framing level, then fails loudly at `iter()` with `OpLogError::Deserialize`; no silent success.

Static grep found no live pre-D-1 patterns. Remaining hits are comments/tests or acceptable raw OOXML boundary checks.

Validation used temporary tests only, then removed them:
`cargo test -p ql-io-xlsx --test codex_d1_step8_tmp -- --nocapture` passed 2/2.
`cargo test -p ql-oplog --test codex_d1_legacy_op_tmp -- --nocapture` passed 1/1.
Sub-agent edge probes passed 3/3, including 1200 multi-peer formats. No tracked source diff remains from the audit probes.

**Verdict**

No HIGH findings. I would not call D-1 fully closed yet because there are two MEDIUM closure items in the XLSX format-overlay boundary.

**MEDIUM 1: XLSX import can create unresolved format overlays**

`cellXfs` styles are applied by converting `xf.num_fmt_id` directly with `legacy_from_u32` and setting the overlay, without checking that custom IDs resolve in `FormatTable`: [lib.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io-xlsx/src/lib.rs:279). The high-ID guard only applies to declared `<numFmt>` entries: [styles_import.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io-xlsx/src/read/styles_import.rs:55).

Empirical result: `<xf numFmtId="999999999">` with no matching `<numFmt>` imports successfully as `Custom(LEGACY_PEER, 999999835)` with no format string. Saving to `.qbook` then reloading fails at the qbook overlay resolver: [qbook_format.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io/src/qbook_format.rs:1752).

**MEDIUM 2: XLSX export accepts unregistered custom overlay IDs**

The exporter includes overlay-used custom IDs in translation even if absent from `workbook.formats()`: [umya_export.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io-xlsx/src/write/umya_export.rs:147). Missing format-code entries allocate a numFmtId anyway: [umya_export.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io-xlsx/src/write/umya_export.rs:225). But `<numFmt>` declarations are emitted only from `workbook.formats()`: [umya_export.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-io-xlsx/src/write/umya_export.rs:553).

Empirical result: an overlay bound to `Custom(PeerId(777), 0)` with no `FormatTable` entry exports an `<xf numFmtId="164">` but no `<numFmt numFmtId="164">`; reimport produces an unresolved overlay.

**LOW: version coupling is documented but not enforced**

`WORKBOOK_SCHEMA_VERSION`, `FormatIdWire` serde shape, and `OPLOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` are pinned separately. Current behavior is okay, but a future `FormatIdWire` shape change has no single test forcing both qbook and oplog schema bumps.
